meta.name: Southampton resident report categories
notes: Team names are OUR labels, not official council team names. team_confirmed is false everywhere until checked with the council.
example_phrases are written by us (synthetic), not copied from FixMyStreet or any resident.
fms_categories are the 26 category names shown on the public FixMyStreet Southampton page (fetched 2026-10-17). They are set by the council, so they can change.

v0.3: only fully confirmed categories kept. Removed (not fully confirmed): road_pavement_defect, manhole_drain, road_signs_markings, street_lighting_traffic_lights, overgrown_vegetation, pests_rats_public, private_rented_disrepair, hmo_concern

duplicate_rule.note: Same rule as CLAUDE.md, implemented in code/tools.py check_duplicate. Location text is compared ignoring case, spacing and punctuation. Resolved reports are never matched. No coordinates are stored, so there is no radius. Window_days is a placeholder, tune it on test data.

outcomes.council_report: Collect required fields, create a report, route to team, give resident a reference number.
outcomes.info_only: Answer from a cited council page (URL + fetch date). No report is created unless the resident asks.
outcomes.not_council: Tell the resident this is not a council responsibility, say who to contact, log it as not_council for evaluation.
outcomes.emergency_redirect: Show official guidance only. Do not write our own safety instructions. Still log a report if the resident wants one.

council_out_of_hours.label: Southampton City Council emergency out of hours

council_roads.label: Southampton City Council: report a pothole or road defect

categories.label: Fly-tipping
example_phrases: someone dumped a sofa by the bins
bags of rubbish left on the verge
mattress dumped in the alley
follow_up_questions: Where exactly is it (street name or nearest house number)?
What has been dumped, and roughly how much?
Can you send a photo?
Is it blocking a path or road?

high: hazardous items such as asbestos, needles, chemicals

categories.form_scope_notes: Private land: owner/occupier resolves it. Report only if on public land, or witnessed with evidence of who did it.

categories.label: Dog fouling
example_phrases: dog mess all along the path
nobody picks up after their dog on our road
follow_up_questions: Which street or park, and which part of it?
Is it a one-off or a regular problem?

high: near a school entrance or play area

categories.label: Dead animal
example_phrases: dead fox on the road
dead bird on the pavement
follow_up_questions: Where exactly is it?
What kind of animal is it (roughly)?
Is it in the road or on the pavement?
categories.form_scope_notes: Council clears on council-owned/managed land. Private land: owner, contact a vet. Ask if it is a traffic hazard on a busy road (high priority).

categories.label: Litter / street needs cleaning
example_phrases: litter everywhere outside the shops
street never gets swept
abandoned shopping trolley
follow_up_questions: Which street and which stretch?
Is it litter, leaves, or something else?
categories.form_scope_notes: Shopping trolleys: tell resident to contact the retailer first. Leaves: only serious hazard or flood risk.

categories.label: Graffiti / fly-posting
example_phrases: graffiti on the wall by the bus stop
posters stuck on every lamp post
follow_up_questions: Where is it, and is it on a council building or private property?
Is it offensive or threatening in content?
categories.form_scope_notes: Private/commercial property not in core service; advise police report (criminal damage). Hate/obscene graffiti is aimed within 1 working day.

categories.label: Broken glass / spillage / dangerous item on the street
example_phrases: broken glass all over the cycle path
oil spill on the road
follow_up_questions: Where exactly is it?
What is it (glass, oil, something else)?
Is it on the road, pavement or cycle path?

categories.label: Pothole
example_phrases: massive crater nearly burst my tyre
hole in the road by the crossing
road surface is breaking up
follow_up_questions: Which road, and nearest house number or junction?
Roughly how big and how deep?
Is it in the road, on a cycle lane, or on the pavement?
Is it a main road or a motorway/trunk road?
categories.check_ownership: If the road is a motorway, or a named trunk or main road (A33, A36 or similar) that the facts do not say the council looks after, switch to not_council_trunk_road.
categories.form_scope_notes: One report per pothole. Needs location, depth, photo if possible. Depth bands: road <4cm monitor, 4-7.5cm 6 months, >7.5cm 24h; pavement <2/2-4/>4cm.

categories.label: Abandoned vehicle
example_phrases: car has not moved for months and has flat tyres
burnt out car left on the street
follow_up_questions: Where is it?
How long has it been there?
Can you see a registration plate, and is it burnt out or damaged?
categories.form_scope_notes: Must not be in use. Reporter needs contact details (DVLA condition), registration, photos. Private land needs signed landowner declaration.

categories.label: Illegal or obstructive parking
example_phrases: car blocking my driveway
cars parked on the pavement
parked on double yellows by the school
follow_up_questions: Where exactly, and what is being blocked (driveway, pavement, junction, crossing)?
What time was it, and does it happen regularly?

high: blocking an emergency route or dropped kerb used by a wheelchair user

categories.form_scope_notes: Dangerous parking with no restriction: police 101. Blocked driveway needs name, address, phone.

categories.label: Noise from a neighbouring property
example_phrases: loud music every night from next door
neighbours shouting late
dog barking all day
follow_up_questions: What kind of noise is it?
What times does it happen, and how often?
How long has it been going on?
Is it a house, flat or HMO?
categories.note: If there are threats or violence, show 999 guidance. Do not handle it as a normal noise report.
categories.form_scope_notes: Check the council's excluded noise list before taking a report; car/motorcycle noise: police first; council needs contact details.

categories.label: Light, dust, smoke or odour from a neighbouring property
example_phrases: neighbour burns rubbish every weekend
floodlight shines into our bedroom
smell from next door
follow_up_questions: What is the problem (light, dust, smoke, smell)?
When does it happen and how often?
categories.form_scope_notes: Council form types include dust, bonfire smoke, smells, security light nuisance, birds.

categories.label: Concern about a property (very dirty, hoarding, possible rodents)
example_phrases: house full of rubbish and rats seen going in
neighbour's garden is piled with junk and smells
follow_up_questions: What is the address or nearest address?
What can you see or smell from outside?
Have you seen rats or other pests?
categories.note: Do not ask for or store the name of the person living there.
categories.form_scope_notes: Types: blocked drains, empty/derelict, filthy, overcrowded, overgrown garden. Speak to owner first.

categories.label: Missed bin collection
example_phrases: bins weren't collected today
they skipped our street again
follow_up_questions: What is your address or postcode?
Which bin was missed (general waste, recycling, glass)?
What was the scheduled collection day?
Was the bin out the right day and clearly visible?
rules_from_council_page: Check the bin was out on the correct day and clearly visible.
Report within two working days of the original collection day.
The council aims to return within two to five working days.
categories.info_first_note: Check the council's conditions before creating a report. If the resident is past the reporting window, explain and point to the page.
categories.form_scope_notes: Council checklist: out on correct day, visible, out by 6:30am, within 2 working days; if due today only after 4pm.

categories.label: Lost, damaged or stray bin
example_phrases: my recycling bin has gone missing
bin lid is broken
follow_up_questions: What is your address?
Which bin is it?
Is it missing or damaged?
Have you checked neighbours and nearby streets?
categories.info_first_note: The council page asks residents to check whether the bin was moved, claimed by a neighbour or returned to the wrong house before reporting.

categories.label: Repair for a council tenant or leaseholder
example_phrases: my council flat has a broken boiler
leak in the ceiling of my council house
follow_up_questions: Is your landlord Southampton City Council?
What is broken and where in the home?
Is it urgent (no heating, water leak, safety)?
categories.note: The council has a separate online form for council tenants and leaseholders, so this must not be mixed up with private rented disrepair.

categories.label: Student question: who deals with bins and rubbish at my house
example_phrases: who is responsible for the bins in my student house
will I get fined if bins stay out
what do I do with my old furniture when I move out
answer_facts_to_cite: Tenants (not landlords) are responsible for making sure household waste is disposed of properly.
Repeatedly leaving bins on the street can lead to a £60 fine.
Everyone in the house shares responsibility for putting the right waste in bins, putting them out, and bringing them back in.
categories.note: Re-fetch the page and confirm the facts and fine amount before the demo. Facts here were read on 2026-10-17.

categories.label: Flooding or severe weather
example_phrases: road is flooded
river is coming up to the houses
storm brought down a tree on the road
follow_up_questions: Where is it?
Is anyone in danger right now?
categories.note: Do not write our own safety instructions. Show the official links first, then offer to log a report.
categories.notes: Not taken as a report. Show official guidance only (999 for danger, Environment Agency flood warnings, council report-a-flood page).

categories.label: Motorway or trunk road problem
example_phrases: pothole on the motorway slip road
streetlight out on the M27
categories.note: If the resident names a trunk or main road (A33, A36 or similar) and the facts do not say who is responsible, say once that we cannot confirm who looks after that road, point them to the council_roads page or National Highways, and do not save a report.
categories.notes: Decided to leave out: A33/A36 responsibility not confirmed.

categories.label: Utility problem (water, gas, electricity, telecoms)
example_phrases: water leak running down the road for weeks
BT cable box open on the pavement
categories.note: We do not yet have verified contact details for each utility. Add them after checking. Until then, tell the resident it is probably the utility company's job and log it as low confidence for officer review.

categories.label: Location is outside Southampton
example_phrases: pothole in Eastleigh
fly-tipping near Totton
categories.note: Demo failure case: location check fails, resident is told it is outside coverage and pointed to the right council.

categories.label: Unclear or other
follow_up_questions: Can you tell me a bit more about what is happening and where?
categories.note: Use when confidence is low or after the conversation limit. Never guess a category. Flag for officer review.

categories.label: A council service the agent does not handle
example_phrases: how do I pay my council tax
I need a blue badge
my taxi complaint
categories.notes: Council runs ~700 services. Give the official online forms page, do not guess. Never create a report.

location_check.rule: Ask where the PROBLEM is, not where the resident lives. Do not decide city boundary from postcode prefix alone.
location_check.evidence: Council address search covers SO14-SO19 only, and some SO16, SO18 and SO19 properties are outside the city boundary.
